PHASE.NAME: UPGRADE_5 OpenTelemetry OTLP Export
PHASE.GOAL: Add optional OpenTelemetry export for tracing hot paths to OTLP-compatible collectors while preserving default stderr-only tracing.

DATA_FLOWS.FLOW: Telemetry config controls enabled state, endpoint, service name, sampling, export interval, and resource attributes.
When disabled, tracing remains JSON stderr only and keeps existing runtime behavior.
When enabled with the telemetry feature, spans export through OTLP and include tool names, adapter routes, token metrics, durations, and error status.
docker-compose.telemetry.yml provides a local Jaeger collector for manual smoke testing.

STEPS.step-1: Add feature-gated OpenTelemetry dependencies and telemetry initialization module.
STEPS.step-2: Add backward-compatible [telemetry] config defaults and typed config key support.
STEPS.step-3: Initialize telemetry once at startup and shut down exporters cleanly when enabled.
STEPS.step-4: Instrument proxy execution with command, adapter, route, input tokens, output tokens, and savings fields.
STEPS.step-5: Instrument tools/call and tools/list paths with tool, session, budget, and context-pressure metadata.
STEPS.step-6: Instrument index and graph hot paths with bounded span fields.

VERIFICATION.CHECK: syn config get telemetry.enabled reports false by default.
With telemetry disabled, syn verify keeps stderr-only tracing.
With telemetry enabled and local Jaeger running, spans reach the OTLP endpoint.

RISKS.RISK: Telemetry dependencies can disturb release portability; keep the feature optional and default-off.
Span fields can leak command arguments; record bounded route metadata and avoid secrets.
